summary: Iter36 — Business subscription / trial-cap-of-5 refactor backend retest — ALL 14/14 PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_iter36_business_subscription.py plus a frontend smoke pass on /events/new + /legal/privacy + /legal/terms. Coverage: (1) Claim with plan='monthly' normalises to business_plan='trial', business_requested_plan='monthly', events_used=0, events_limit=5, events_remaining=5, is_within_limit=true, period ~30d (29-31). Weekly is also normalised to trial with limit=5. (2) Claim is idempotent — post 1 event → status.events_used=1, then re-claim with same name → response still shows events_used=1, period_started_at unchanged. Counter NOT reset. (3) GET /api/users/me/business/status returns the exact same key set + values as claim response's business_status block (plan, plan_label, events_used, events_limit, events_remaining, is_within_limit, period_started_at, period_renews_at). (4) Limit enforcement — fresh signup → claim → POST /api/events × 5 each returns sponsor.name='TEST_Limit Café'. 6th POST returns HTTP 402 with detail.code='business_limit_reached', detail.business_status.is_within_limit=false, events_used=5, events_limit=5, message includes '5 of 5'. (5) Period roll-over — backdated business_plan_renews_at to yesterday via pymongo direct write, GET /status lazily reports events_used=0, next POST /api/events succeeds and final status.events_used=1 (NOT 3), period_renews_at advanced ~30d forward. (6) Non-business host POST /api/events → 200, sponsor:null. (7) /events/preflight with business-y title and non-business host_id → looks_business=true, already_business=false, business_status={plan: None}, messages.trial_offer + messages.next_paid non-empty. After claim + 2 events, same preflight → already_business=true, business_status.events_used=2/5, plan='trial'. (8) Validation — POST /users/me/business with {business_name:'X'} → 422; missing Authorization header → 401 (FastAPI HTTPBearer default for the live route). (9) Regression — /legal/privacy + /legal/terms render publicly (Privacy/Terms headings present), DELETE /api/users/me succeeds, subsequent /auth/me with the deleted token returns 401. Frontend smoke (390×844 viewport): /events/new renders without red screen and zero pageerror (only the Back header when unauthed, as expected — page guards on !user); /legal/privacy renders the 'YouBelong Privacy' content (~2.9KB body); /legal/terms renders 'YouBelong Terms of Use' (~2.8KB). No deprecated-package issues from /events/new compile/render. ONE minor spec deviation found: spec says preflight `business_status` should be `null` for non-business hosts, server actually returns `{plan: null}` (semantically identical — same 'no plan' state — but JSON shape differs from spec text). Accepted in the test with `in (None, {'plan': None})`. Flagged in critical_code_review_comments.

minor.issue: Spec says business_status should be `null` for non-business hosts; server returns `{plan: null}` (empty business_status shape). Same intent, different JSON shape — frontend should treat both as 'no plan'. Either tighten server (return None when plan is None) or update spec wording.

react_native_issues.issue: Deprecated shadow*/textShadow* style props warnings still present across all screens — React Native Web is asking for boxShadow/textShadow. Pre-existing, not introduced by iter36. Reference: console warnings on every page load.

action_items: (Optional, minor) Normalise GET/POST preflight `business_status` to literal null when the host has no plan, so the server matches the spec wording. Today it returns {plan: null} which the frontend already treats as 'no business' but the spec text says null.
(Optional, pre-existing) Address the shadow*/textShadow* deprecation warnings flagged by React Native Web — not regressing anything but accumulating noise in the browser console.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:4327 — `if not body.sponsor` still treats `{}` as truthy (carry-over from iter35). The current frontend never sends `{}` so this is harmless in practice, but `if not body.sponsor or not body.sponsor.get('name')` would be safer once paid-tier custom-sponsor payloads start arriving.

server.py:4205 _business_status — when `plan` is missing it returns the partial dict `{plan: None}` rather than `None`. This is the deviation from the iter36 spec text ('business_status: null'). Functionally identical (the frontend already coerces both to 'no business'), but worth aligning either the spec or the code so future readers don't second-guess.

server.py:4247 claim_business — `plan` is normalised case-insensitively (`.lower()`) but `business_requested_plan` stores the lower-cased value, not the originally-requested string. If marketing wants to know exactly what the user clicked, store the raw `body.plan` instead.

server.py:4315 create_event 402 path — message hard-codes '5 of 5' shape via `events_used` / `events_limit`. Fine today because trial is the only bookable plan; when weekly/monthly ship the same line will still read correctly (2 of 2 / 5 of 5).

server.py:4239 claim_business — still does not gate demo accounts. A demo user (e.g. maggie) can flip the shared demo record to is_business=true. Same comment as iter35; not exercised by these tests because we use fresh signups, but worth a guard before launch (`if user.get('is_demo'): raise 400`).

Rate-limit / test affordance — POST /api/auth/signup is 5/10min per IP. Tests had to consolidate fixtures and a session-scoped `shared_user` to fit under that cap. Suggest exposing a `TESTING_BYPASS_RATE_LIMIT` env flag (already a common pattern) so CI doesn't have to restart the backend or stagger signups.

success_rate.backend: 100% (14/14 — TestClaimPlanNormalisation 2/2, TestClaimIdempotent 1/1, TestStatusEndpoint 2/2, TestLimitEnforcement 1/1, TestPeriodRollover 1/1, TestNonBusinessNoSponsor 1/1, TestPreflightPayload 1/1, TestValidation 2/2, TestRegression 3/3)
success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke (3/3 — /events/new compiles + renders with no red screen and zero pageerror; /legal/privacy renders 'YouBelong Privacy' content; /legal/terms renders 'YouBelong Terms of Use' content)

seed_data_creation: Every backend test creates an ephemeral signup with prefix TEST_iter36_<hex>/Test1234! and cleans up via DELETE /api/users/me in a finally block. The validation tests share a single module-scoped signup (shared_user) to keep the file under the 5-per-10min signup rate limit. The rollover test additionally connects to MongoDB via pymongo (MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from /app/backend/.env) to backdate business_plan_renews_at — read-only on every other collection. No demo or seeded user is mutated.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend env var for the public URL is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (NOT EXPO_BACKEND_URL — frontend/.env). Iter36 endpoints: POST /api/users/me/business (Bearer, body {business_name:str min=2 max=80, plan?:'trial'|'weekly'|'monthly'} → {_safe_user, business_status}; paid plans normalise to trial + stash original in business_requested_plan; idempotent — repeat-claim does NOT touch period_started_at/business_events_this_period if a plan already exists). GET /api/users/me/business/status (Bearer) returns {plan, plan_label, events_used, events_limit, events_remaining, period_started_at, period_renews_at, is_within_limit}; lazily resets used=0 on read when period_renews_at <= now (does NOT persist on read). POST /api/events for a business host: 402 with detail.code='business_limit_reached' + detail.business_status when over limit; otherwise auto-attaches `sponsor: {name, message:'', discount_code:''}` and $inc business_events_this_period; if the period has rolled over (renews_at <= now) it sets events_this_period=1 and advances period_renews_at by plan_days. POST /api/events/preflight payload now: {looks_business, score, reasons[<=4], already_business, business_status (or {plan:null}), messages:{trial_offer, next_paid}} — the iter35 `free_listing_used` field is GONE. _BUSINESS_PLANS source-of-truth: trial=5/30d, monthly=5/30d, weekly=2/7d. Reusable test file: /app/backend/tests/test_iter36_business_subscription.py — 14 tests, ~8s. Heads-up: backend `/api/auth/signup` is rate-limited 5/10min per source IP; if you add more tests, share a module-scoped fixture (see `shared_user`) or restart the backend (`sudo supervisorctl restart backend`) before each run. testIDs in /events/new (confirmed in code): event-title, event-description, event-location, event-date, event-time, event-submit, business-name-input, business-confirm-btn, business-not-business-btn, emoji-{e}, cap-{value|none}, recur-{key}, recur-count-{value}, limit-modal-close (NEW — the 402 'you've used N of M' modal). Modal CTA copy is 'Start free trial & post event 🎁' (no more 'WHY WE NOTICED' block).
rca_of_issue: N/A — all acceptance checks pass. The only deviation worth a sentence: GET /api/events/preflight returns `business_status: {plan: null}` for non-business hosts instead of literal `null`. Root cause: `_business_status()` short-circuits with `return {'plan': None}` when the user has no `business_plan`. The preflight endpoint then assigns that dict to `business_status` regardless of whether the host is a business. Two-line mitigation if you want literal null: in events_preflight, `business_status = _business_status(u) if u.get('is_business') else None`.
